definition: Misogyny is prejudiced, demeaning, or discriminatory attitudes and behaviour directed at girls or women. In this packet, online misogyny refers to such views being promoted through social media and reflected in comments, influencer praise, and harmful treatment of female peers or staff.

reasons: The packet does not provide an explicit general definition of misogyny as “prejudiced, demeaning, or discriminatory attitudes and behaviour directed at girls or women.”
The packet uses the phrase “online misogyny” but does not substantiate the specific wording that it is “directed at girls or women.”

The second sentence adds specific elements (“influencer praise” and “harmful treatment of female peers or staff”) that are only described indirectly by teachers’ examples; the packet does not define these as the core components of misogyny itself (it reports perceptions/examples in schools).
The overall definition includes claims not stated as definitions within the packet, beyond reporting that teachers referenced certain behaviours they attributed to online misogyny.

The packet supports online misogyny in schools, but not the broader dictionary claim that misogyny is generally prejudiced, demeaning, or discriminatory attitudes and behaviour directed at girls or women.

The packet does not support the definitional generalization beyond the school-based examples of misogynistic comments, praise of misogynistic influencers, and discriminatory behaviour toward female peers and staff.
